name: The Old Wild Apple Tree of Žiar

location.address: On the hill known as Diel, above the village of Žiar, Liptovský Mikuláš District, Žilina Region, Slovakia
location.neighbourhood: Diel hillside, Žiar (roughly 15 km from Veľké Borové)

access: Open hillside farmland above Žiar village, at 860 m elevation, at the edge of a field on the hill called Diel. No source records a gate, fee or restriction, and a marked cycling route in the area passes close by, but this is working agricultural land rather than a park: reach it on foot or by bike along the farm track up the hillside and stay to the field edge.
transport: No public transport to the tree itself. Car or bike to Žiar village (on the L. Mikuláš side of the Western Tatras, near the popular Žiarska dolina trailhead), then on foot or by bike up the hillside track to Diel, roughly 15 km / 20-25 minutes' drive from Veľké Borové plus the walk up.
verify_notes: 2026 European Tree of the Year, rank 2 (runner-up), 4,766 tree points, beaten only by Lithuania's Oak of Laukiai. Won Slovakia's own 'Strom roka 2025' (Tree of the Year) contest first, with 4,345 of over 18,000 votes cast, beating a beech from Cechanky and a lime from Krasny Brod; that qualified it for the European final. Contest organiser is Nadacia Ekopolis (Ekopolis Foundation), which runs the Slovak leg; the Slovak press agency TASR and multiple outlets (teraz.sk, Pravda, Bystricoviny) covered both the national and European rounds independently of Ekopolis's own materials. Species: Malus sylvestris, European wild apple/crab apple, confirmed by name in every source; a genuinely unusual entrant since ornamental/cultivated species and oaks/limes/beeches dominate these contests. Measurements (bystricoviny.sk, quoting Ekopolis's own tree card): girth 242 cm at breast height, height about 8 m, age approx. 150 years (source's own figure; age_basis 'source', not derived by us). GPS 49.1297028, 19.6786144 given directly by the source alongside the measurements, matching the contest page's GPS (N49 7'46.93'' E19 40'43.01'') and matching the nomination via Viera Kacerova, who lives locally. STORY, the reason this small tree is worth a page: it stands alone at the far edge of a field that generations of villagers worked by hand, on a windswept shoulder of the Western Tatras foothills at 860 m, and nobody knows for certain how it got there -- accounts say it may have grown from a chance seed a bird carried, or from windfall from a discarded apple core, rather than being deliberately planted. It has survived over 150 years of mountain wind, frost and drought completely untended: no orchard care, no protection, 'just its own vitality' (TASR/Pravda). A resident quoted in Pravda: 'Uz moj stary otec si ju pamatal z detstva. A dnes chodim k nej ja' (Even my grandfather remembered it from his childhood. And today I go to it) -- three generations visiting the same tree as a place of quiet. The Ekopolis Foundation's own framing: the competition exists 'not because of records, but because of the relationship between people and nature' that trees like this represent. Slovakia's best-ever European result is 3rd place in 2016 (a pear tree from Bosaca-Zabudisova); this apple placed 2nd, the country's best result to date. ACCESS CAVEAT for the writer: nothing found describes a formal gate or fee, and it sits near the well-used Ziarska dolina family hiking valley, but sources describe it as standing on farmland at a field's edge rather than in a designated public park, so the honest framing is 'on open hillside farmland, no restriction found' rather than 'a public garden'. DISTANCE CAVEAT: Ziar/Diel is a separate hillside stop roughly 15 km from Velke Borove's existing tree (vbo_001, the Pine of Velke Borove); it is a drive-then-walk day out, not a joint stroll with the existing tree.
